evidence: Rule-based screens, not advice. Live track record so far: 3 overlapping weekly batches, average rank correlation +0.05 — not yet enough independent history to call it skill.
method: Chosen by rule from the scores on this page, not by hand: fundamentally strong (for stocks, a multi-year record over up to six years: profitable in at least 80% of them, revenue and earnings up in at least 60% with positive growth rates and no boom-bust swings; growth at least median vs peers, counting how steady it was as much as how fast), plausible data, and not in the most expensive 20% — then ranked by opportunity score. Stocks also need a market cap of at least $2B, US-dollar financial statements, a US domicile (foreign listings' share counts don't yet account for ADR ratios), at least 3 years of reported history, and no open data-quality issue.

deep_value_intact.label: Deep discount, fundamentals intact
deep_value_intact.rule: Quality on sale, at least 20% below its long-run average, and cheap (value score 60+).

on_sale.label: Quality on sale
on_sale.rule: Profitable, revenue and earnings growing, not expensive vs peers — and trading at least 10% below its 5-year average price (or its average over all the price history on file, if shorter).

steady_on_sale.label: Steady compounder on sale
steady_on_sale.rule: Quality on sale with a steady record: revenue and earnings up in at least 80% of the last six years, profitable every year, and low year-to-year volatility.

turning_up.label: Quality on sale, turning up
turning_up.rule: Quality on sale where the fall looks to have stopped: up over the last month and back at least 15% off its 52-week low.
